name: Chanterelle

facts.when: Summer, one to two weeks after soaking rains
facts.where: Oak woods in East Texas, on soil, never on wood

caution: The jack-o'-lantern mushroom is the dangerous double: it grows in clusters ON wood and has true gills. Chanterelles grow from soil with blunt false ridges. Mushrooms demand expert confirmation; when in doubt, throw it out.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Hunt oak woods a week after summer rain. Cut or pinch at the base, brush off the leaf litter, and carry them in a basket so the woods get their spores back.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Dry-sauté first to drive off water, then add butter. The apricot smell survives cooking and makes these the East Texas prize.
